profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility at 2220 De La Cruz Boulevard, Santa Clara, CA, per mapping data. Digital Realty's Silicon Valley metro listing includes a property at 220 De La Cruz Boulevard (SC1); this session's fetch did not confirm whether that record or a separate one corresponds to this specific 2220 address, so no operator-confirmed square footage is reported here rather than assuming the two are the same building.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building sits within Digital Realty's Silicon Valley campus, a dense cluster of buildings across Santa Clara and Santa Clara County that is one of the company's oldest US footprints, reflecting the area's history as a birthplace of the commercial colocation and internet exchange industry. Digital Realty's own Silicon Valley metro page, fetched this session, lists numerous named properties concentrated along Comstock Street, Lafayette Street, and Walsh Avenue, ranging from under 15,000 to nearly 400,000 square feet each.

Digital Realty markets its Silicon Valley properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company's FY2025 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage.

PG&E is the principal electric utility serving most of the area, and California's data center growth has drawn scrutiny over grid capacity and water use for cooling in recent years. reading.body:
Digital Realty's De La Cruz Boulevard facility in Santa Clara is a 471,000 square foot colocation building in one of the company's densest US footprints, serving the Silicon Valley metro alongside dozens of other named properties concentrated within Santa Clara County. The operator does not publish a megawatt IT capacity figure for this building on its property page or in its SEC filings, which report only aggregate portfolio metrics by region rather than per-building power ratings. Without a published IT load, the campus's AI significance cannot be assessed from operator disclosures alone.

The facility operates under Digital Realty's PlatformDIGITAL brand as a wholesale colocation landlord, meaning it hosts customer compute rather than running its own infrastructure. Silicon Valley's data center cluster, anchored by Santa Clara and San Jose, sits on PG&E's grid and has drawn scrutiny over capacity and water use as the region's computing intensity has grown. The area also hosts major campuses for Google, Meta, and other hyperscaler and enterprise tenants.

Within California's mapped data center footprint of 103 facilities, only 11 publish megawatt figures, totaling 365 MW. This facility does not publish capacity and therefore cannot be ranked by power within the state. Its utility to AI scaling depends on published tenant commitments, grid connection specifications, and colocation pricing, none of which are disclosed in operator spec pages read to date.
